content.title: Religion within the Boundary of Pure Reason (1793; English translation 1838)
content.author: Immanuel Kant · translated by J. W. Semple (Edinburgh: Thomas Clark, 1838)
content.role: Primary record · not a teaching authority
content.note: Kant's account of religion within the limits of moral reason. Book II, section I argues that guilt is the most personal of debts, payable only by the guilty and never by an innocent substitute. Cited for that objection, not as teaching. Public domain (published 1838).
content.read: Read online on 2026-11-27 in the Internet Archive's text of Semple's 1838 translation: Book II, section I, the passage on the third difficulty (pp. 87-88), that the debt of sin is not transferable like a money debt. 2026-11-27 (plan APOLOGETICS-FIELDS step 6, held copy): the same Internet Archive text downloaded by the job to sources/archive-org/kant-religion-semple-1838.txt (checksum in Website/SOURCES.md, 'Apologetics fields: the step-6 samples'); the passages above were read in this file too.
